ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities was $179 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared to $184 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025. There was a decrease of $31 million associated with net decoupling deferrals and amortizations, primarily associated with decoupling surcharges recognized in the first quarter of 2026 due to milder weather and decreased customer usage. Changes in other current liabilities and accounts payable decreased operating cash flows by $37 million compared to the first quarter of 2025, primarily due to the timing of a litigation settlement accrual during the first quarter of 2025, as well as decreased payables for natural gas purchases as volumes purchased in 2026 decreased. These decreases were partially offset by the change in other current assets, which increased operating cash flows by $60 million, due to timing of prepayments and insurance proceeds receivables recorded during the first quarter of 2025.

da.text: Utility depreciation and amortization decreased primarily due to our exit from Colstrip in 2026. In anticipation of the exit, we had accelerated depreciation, as we were required to recover costs from Washington customers by the end of 2025.

wc.text: A $7 million increase in other gas revenues primarily due to the amortization of previously deferred revenues associated with the sale of CCA emissions credits. We amortize the deferred revenues as they are passed on to customers through decreases in retail rates. The increase in other revenues was offset by decreased retail rates as discussed above, resulting in no impact to utility margin. This increase was partially offset by a decrease in transportation revenue, as well as a provision for rate refunds associated with overearnings in Washington recorded in the first quarter of 2026.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The realization of many of the risks discussed herein depends upon the prior occurrence of some event or circumstance – i.e. a “trigger”.
Our ability to recover these expenses and capital costs depends on the adequacy and timeliness of retail rate increases allowed by regulatory agencies, as well as managing costs.

We rely on interconnected technology systems for operation of our generating plants, electric transmission and distribution systems, natural gas distribution systems, customer billing and customer service, accounting and other administrative processes and compliance with various regulations.
We rely on regular access to financial markets, but we cannot assure favorable or reasonable financing terms will be available when we need them.
We rely on credit from financial institutions for short-term borrowings.
We rely on energy markets and other counterparties for energy supply, surplus and optimization transactions and commodity price hedging.
We rely on a variety of generation and energy commodity market sources to fulfill our obligation to serve customers and meet the demands of our counterparty agreements.

If the northwest region does not build sufficient new generation capacity and additional transmission and gas transport, there is a risk that we will not be able to depend on excess energy market purchases to meet customer demand during extreme weather events.
The primary source of operating cash flows for Avista Utilities is revenues from sales of electricity and natural gas.

Advances in power generation, energy efficiency, energy storage and other alternative energy technologies could lead to more wide-spread usage of these technologies, thereby reducing customer demand for the energy supplied by us.

The amount of potential default risk from each counterparty depends on the duration and volume of our obligations under forward contracts, unsettled transactions, interest rates and market prices, as well as other factors.

To manage the impacts of volatile natural gas prices, we procure natural gas through a diversified mix of spot market purchases and forward fixed price purchases from various supply basins and time periods.
